segments.t: Outside the ASK agency, Andrea Martel receives an unexpected visit from Colette Brancillon, who brings baby Flora in a stroller. Surprised and deeply touched, Andrea takes her daughter into her arms for a joyful reunion. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Colette! Qu'est-ce que tu fais là?
On se promenait dans le quartier.
Tu as amené Flora avec toi?
Oui, elle voulait voir sa mère.
C'est une très belle surprise!
Je sais que tu travailles beaucoup.
Oui, mais vous me manquez tellement.
Prends-la dans tes bras maintenant.
Viens avec maman, mon petit trésor.
Elle te sourit avec bonheur.
Tu es si douce, ma Flora.
Allons faire un tour au parc.
Oui, avec grand plaisir, Colette.
Prenons le temps de nous poser.
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Colette! Qu'est-ce que tu fais là?
'Colette! What are you doing here?' Andrea is stunned to see Colette outside ASK. The question phrase 'qu'est-ce que' asks what.
On se promenait dans le quartier.
'We were taking a walk in the neighborhood.' Colette explains why she is nearby. The reflexive verb 'ourselves' means to take a walk.
Tu as amené Flora avec toi?
'You brought Flora with you?' Andrea looks down happily at the stroller. The compound past 'have' comes from 'brought', to bring someone.
Oui, elle voulait voir sa mère.
'Yes, she wanted to see her mother.' This everyday French sentence pairs 'yes' with 'mother'.
C'est une très belle surprise!
'It is a very wonderful surprise!' Andrea feels a wave of relief and joy. The feminine noun 'surprise' designates an unexpected event.
Je sais que tu travailles beaucoup.
'I know that you work a lot.' Colette acknowledges Andrea's busy schedule. The adverb 'beaucoup' indicates a large amount.
Oui, mais vous me manquez tellement.
'Yes, but I miss you both so much.' Andrea expresses her heartfelt longing. The structure 'you' literally translates to you are missing to me.
Prends-la dans tes bras maintenant.
'Take her in your arms now.' Colette gently unbuckles Flora from the stroller. The plural noun 'arms' means arms.
Viens avec maman, mon petit trésor.
'Come with mommy, my little treasure.' Andrea lifts baby Flora into her arms. The noun 'treasure' is an affectionate term of endearment.
Elle te sourit avec bonheur.
'She smiles at you with happiness.' Colette links 'she' directly with 'at you' to express the thought clearly. Then Andréa responds.
Tu es si douce, ma Flora.
'You are so sweet, my Flora.' Andrea holds her daughter close against her chest. The feminine adjective 'sweet' means gentle or sweet.
Allons faire un tour au parc.
'Let us take a walk in the park.' Colette suggests stepping away from the office. The imperative 'let us go' invites shared action.
Oui, avec grand plaisir, Colette.
'Yes, with great pleasure, Colette.' Andrea agrees gladly to spend time together. The noun 'pleasure' means pleasure or delight.
Prenons le temps de nous poser.

'Let us take the time to pause.' Colette leads the way toward the park bench. The reflexive verb 'se poser' means to settle down or rest. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

On se promenait dans le quartier.
Tu as amené Flora avec toi?
Oui, elle voulait voir sa mère.
C'est une très belle surprise!

Oui, mais vous me manquez tellement.
Prends-la dans tes bras maintenant.

Elle te sourit avec bonheur.

Oui, avec grand plaisir, Colette.
Prenons le temps de nous poser.

Reunited in the peaceful Parisian sunshine, Andrea and Colette set off together toward the nearby park. Holding Flora in her arms, Andrea feels grounded after weeks of intense workplace pressure. Now let's listen to the scene one last time.
C'est si bon d'être réunies!
